question: when a later observation implicitly invalidates an earlier memory (no explicit negation), does the memory layer resolve it, or does stale content still reach recall?
protocol: 25 scenarios on fresh service+store: seed one personal fact -> a later-session observation that supersedes it implicitly (moving/changing without saying 'no longer') -> neutral probe question; outcome by marker presence in top-8 orchestrated recall.
findings: The memory layer never resolves implicit invalidation: zero scenarios surfaced only the new value.

52% of probes feed BOTH the stale and the fresh value into recall - correctness is outsourced to model-side arbitration, matching the STALE-paper failure mode (frontier models judge stored-memory validity at ~55%).
44% of probes surface only the stale value: pure invalid reuse.
This is the baseline for the premise-resistance orchestration leg (B2) and for AGM-style belief-revision acceptance criteria on improve.py: target = resolved up, stale_reuse+both down.
honest_reading: recall-marker protocol, no answerer in the loop; temporal.py's explicit supersede path is not exercised because the scenarios deliberately contain no explicit contradiction signal. Default offline profile (tfidf embedder, rule-based extractor).
